title: Graceful admission damper and quick-rejoin hotfix
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Backported a hotfix that smooths admission spikes and shortens tenant quick-rejoin windows; safe to roll to production immediately.
description: Context: During a recent regional instability incident customers observed oscillating admissions and rapid circuit reopen cycles that caused repeated short-lived failures for warm tenants. This PR introduces an admission damper that rate-limits instantaneous admission bursts per-region and a quick-rejoin soft-window that prevents aggressive KV rebinds for recently-evacuated tenants. Motivation: Reduce oscillation and wasted work during transient regional load spikes while preserving fast recovery for healthy traffic. Changes are conservative and gated behind a runtime flag with a default-on safe configuration for production. Checklist: - [x] Add admission damper logic in admission controller - [x] Add quick-rejoin TTL and backoff hook in connection manager - [x] Telemetry: new metrics (admission_damped_count, quick_rejoin_blocked_count) - [x] Unit tests and integration test harness run locally - [x] Canary rollout plan documented in PR - [x] Backported small runtime fix to connection reaper Related: ENG-2841, ENG-2907, incident SUP-912. Deployment notes: enable runtime flag rollout in Canary region for 1 hour, monitor admission_damped_count and per-tenant SLO regression dashboards. If 95th latency or error-rate regressions >0.5% within the window, rollback flag. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-2841/design, incident notes https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-912

patch_summary: Key behavioral surface: - admission controller now tracks short-term admission bursts per region and applies a token-leaky dampening window for bursty clients. - connection manager tracks tenants that evacuated within last N seconds and prevents KV rebind attempts (quick-rejoin) for a short, configurable soft window. - metrics and alerts added; conservative defaults chosen to avoid blocking healthy recovery.
review_thread: Derek Lin (review) - Please confirm the damper's token bucket parameters are safe for very small tenants; we don't want to starve low-traffic customers.
Priya Shah (author) - Adjusted min tokens to 1 and added unit test to assert small-tenant progress; see second commit.
Marina Alvarez (review) - Can you add a short-circuit flag for emergency rollback? We should be able to disable the damper globally via runtime flag.
Priya Shah (author) - Added runtime_flags.yaml entry and admin API hook for immediate disable; documented rollback steps in canary guide.
Conor O'Neill (approval) - Verified metrics and smoke tests in staging; LGTM once CI passes.
canary_plan: Canary in us-west-2 for 60 minutes against low-traffic tenants, then expand to 3 regions over 4 hours. Monitor admission_damped_count, quick_rejoin_blocked_count, 95th latency, and error-rate. Rollback flag available in runtime_flags.yaml.
postmortem_followup: If stabilization observed, schedule follow-up to tune damper parameters and add per-tenant exemptions for VIP customers (ENG-2960). If regressions, revert runtime flag and follow SUP-912 escalation path.
notes_on_backport: Small connection reaper race fix was backported to release/2026.02 as part of this PR; backport patch is minimal and tested.
observability_changes: Added metrics: admission_damped_count{region,tenant}, quick_rejoin_blocked_count{region}; added dashboard tile and alert with threshold tuned to historical variance.
testing_summary: Local unit tests cover damper edge cases and quick-rejoin TTL handling. Integration harness run against simulated region spike scenario showed 45% reduction in admission churn and eliminated repeated reopen cycles in 3/3 runs.
security_considerations: No new auth surfaces. Admin runtime flag uses existing RBAC controls. Reviewed for potential denial-of-service amplification; rate cap enforced per-tenant and per-region.
operational_runbook_snippet: If canary shows unexpected client stall: 1) set runtime flag disabled via admin API 2) restart admission-worker in that region only 3) open incident channel and tag SRE on-call 4) collect admission_damped_count and recent connection logs for triage.
motivating_incident: Incident SUP-912: rapid regional admission oscillation leading to higher error rates for tenants touching the slowpath. This PR resolves the immediate oscillation vector and reduces load during transient healing.
